paper_title: 1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge   Aggregators
caption: Statistics of the dataset in our experiments.
model_annotation: This pie chart displays the distribution of data within a dataset used for experiments, categorized by source. The chart contains five slices representing different data sources. The largest slice, labeled “TriviaQA” and colored red, represents 46% of the data (1829 instances). The next largest slice is labeled “WebQA” and is purple, representing 25% of the data (997 instances). “Chinese Domain” is represented by a tan slice with 6% of the data (231 instances). “HalluEval” is shown as a dark green slice with 18% of the data (721 instances), and “HalluQA” is represented by a smaller, light green slice at 5% of the data (85 instances). Percentage labels and instance counts are displayed inside each slice, and a legend is present in the upper right corner. The slices appear to be arranged in descending order based on their percentage representation.
